utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We are, Your Honours. That would be Mr. Milenko Karisik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I put on the record that Mr. Mladic is back with us in court again. Were you saluting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Karisik. Mr. Karisik, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You'll find Mr. Ivetic to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps with the assistance of the usher, I can have a clean copy of the witness statement shown to opposing counsel while I start with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Could I ask you to first please state your full name for purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I am Milenko Karisik.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And did you give a statement to the Defence team of Radovan Karadzic in 2013?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: My answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to call up in e-court the document, 1D4749a.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, looking at the first page of this document that's on the screen on the left-hand side, do you recognise this statement?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise my own statement. But I would like to ask you to enlarge the letters a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: While we do that, could we also go to the last page of the same in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, looking again at the Serbian original, can you tell us whose signature appears on this page?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That is my signature. My shorter signature. And it is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so the date that is reflected in the left-hand side of the document, is that in accordance with your recollection of what date you signed the statement in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: My answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you stand by everything as written in this statement as being accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: My answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you today questions on the same topics as contained in your statement, would your answers in court today be substantially the same information as is contained in your written statement that we have before us?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Today my answers would confirm the statements I made on that day.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, in so far as you have taken a solemn declaration this morning, can we then consider the answers as contained in your statement to be truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, my answers are truthful. The answers contained in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would at this time then tender 1D4749a as the next Defence exhibit, and there are seven associated documents that also are being tendered at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are they all already on your 65 ter list?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are, Your Honours, and the corresponding Mr. Mladic 65 ter numbers are provided in the chart that was filed with the statement in the 92 ter submission of the Defence, linking them to the Karadzic 65 ter numbers which are present in the statement itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't oppose admission of the statement, but there are four of the associated exhibits that we do oppose -- object to, we indicated as much in our filing of the 9th of February, it's the numbers 1D05309, 05310, 05311, and 05312, for the broad reasons stated in our filing of 9th February, paragraph 3. And I'll just elaborate the first one, 05309. It's mentioned at paragraph 19 of the statement we oppose admission of this document. It's a third-party statement in BiH State Court proceedings. In our submission, admission should be sought under the appropriate Rule of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. In any event, it's not sufficiently explained or commented upon in the relevant paragraph 19. So far as the next one is concerned, that's 05310, it's cited to at paragraph 17 of the witness statement. It's a lengthy book extract not sufficiently explained or commented upon in paragraph 17 of the witness statement. Next one, 1D05311, it's at paragraph 25 of the statement. It doesn't provide -- that paragraph doesn't provide any comment or contextualisation of what is a compilation of SRNA, that's the Serbian press agency's press releases. And the same applies 1D05312, paragraph 25 again. Again in relation to these, no comment or contextualisation of any of these press releases from the Serbian press agency. So we object to the admissions of those four documents as associated exhibits on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me first have a look at the transcript. I think initially, I don't know whether it was --- whether you misspoke or whether it's not accurately recorded, but we are talking about 5309, 5310, 5311, and 5312.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no objections against the other ones. We'll delay our decision on the ones you mentioned and see how the examination of the witness develops in that respect. Could you take the other ones one by one, Mr. Ivetic, so that we can decide on admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. The other ones would be in this order: 1D04751.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number D932, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Next one would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Next one would be 1D5313.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D933, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D934 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then the statement is 1D4749a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D935 is admitted into evidence. Yes, I am still a bit confused that they were all already on your 65 ter list or whether you asked them to be added to the 65 ter list, Mr. Ivetic. I think you said they were already but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have the table from the 92 ter filing but I don't have the filing itself. I assume that they were based upon the fact that they already had Mladic numbers, but looking at them now they're higher than I would have anticipated, so it is possible that they might ones that we sought admission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be very practical. I heard of no objections against them being added to the 65 ter list to the extent it had not been done yet, and therefore your tendering of the documents is understood as implicitly also asking to have them added to the 65 ter list to the extent they were not yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honours. And I'm just looking back at the filings and there were -- six of these seven exhibits were sought to add as onto the 65 ter list and we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was on my mind when I earlier asked Mr. Ivetic whether they were all already on the 65 ter list. But let's not make too much fuss about that at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this time I have the public summary to be ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Milenko Karisik became a member of the special unit of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Ministry of Interior in 1983 and remained as a member of the same until the outbreak of the war. He served as the deputy commander of the special anti-terrorist unit when the war broke out. This unit was the most professionally organised part of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Special attention was paid to ensure that the staffing structure of the unit corresponded to that of the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina; that is to say, the percentage of Serbs, Croats, and Muslims. After the multi-party elections of 1990, the SDA started appointing personnel to key supervisory positions in the Ministry of Interior who used the ministry as a tool to achieve the goals and implement directives of the SDA. Reserve police forces, mostly Muslims, were activated at all levels, including in the special unit. The witness notes that the special anti-terrorist unit started to be tasked to perform tasks that were not within its remit, where the unit was misused with disproportionate strength in unlawful actions in service to intimidate Serbs. These were ordered by the minister, following the orders of the SDA. In the special unit anti-terrorism training stopped and a complete transition was made to military training. This demonstrated a preparation of the unit for new purposes. In the meantime, the recruitment of special reserve police led to the formation of a special reserve unit which occupied some of the buildings of the witness's unit. Only Muslims were recruited into this unit, and for the most part they were from the region of Sandzak, volunteers for the Green Berets, and deserters from the JNA. As a result of the abuses in the use of the special unit, Serbian members, led by the witness, demanded a meeting with the MUP leadership in order to eliminate problems because further work was unbearable and impossible. A meeting was held including Momcilo Mandic, a Serb, Jusuf Pusina, a Muslim, and Bruno Stojic, a Croat, that ended in agreement to put an end to further abuse, but this agreement was not respected by the Muslims. Eventually the MUP was split, and based on an agreement at the top level of the MUP, the Serb special unit was to be assigned to the base in Vrace, whereas the Muslim/Croat part of the unit was to remain in Krtelje. When the Serb unit set out for its assigned base, it was attacked from two directions. It was learned that the leadership of the Muslim MUP ordered this attack. During the unit's stay in Vrace, it was attacked with infantry, anti-armour, and mortar weapons on a daily basis by the Muslim forces. The special unit grew into the special police brigade of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which numbered 1500 personnel with the witness as its commander. The witness states that no one ever asked him or demanded that he as the commander commit a war crime. Later, as chief of the public security department of the MUP of Republika Srpska, the witness never saw any mention of execution of prisoners from Srebrenica in any written reports and himself had no information on the same. And this completes the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further questions for the witness, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to page 2 in both languages of your written statement, and I'd like to ask you about paragraph 8. Now, here you are talking about how the SDA appointed its personnel to key positions in the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that these persons then used that ministry to achieve goals and directives of the SDA. How did the other ethnic groups and ethnic parties react to these actions of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That was the period after the multi-party elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina when the three ruling parties - the SDA, the HDZ, and the SDS - on the basis of the agreement reached -- I mean, I'm a speaking about the Ministry of Interior now, but I imagine this was the situation at all levels of government. This agreement was implemented by a division of portfolios in the government. As for the MUP itself, they, the SDA, got the position of the minister of the interior, one of the most important positions in the then-government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And not only that. On the basis of that agreement, they got other top positions. The assistant minister for police was also a Muslim. The assistant minister for personnel likewise. And now I cannot recall exactly the entire structure, the entire personnel structure, but the most posts through which force could be implemented in the Ministry of Interior, I think I should put it that way, it was Muslims who held these positions and who were appointed to these positions. Of course, Minister Delimustafic, who even had a criminal record, was appointed by political structures and not a professional in the MUP. Minister Delimustafic did not know much about police work, but he knew, that I think for sure, and it was confirmed later, he knew how to convey the orders issued by the SDA that had appointed him in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Mr. Ivetic, I think you asked the witness how other ethnic groups and the ethnic parties reacted to those actions. Now the witness is describing in detail, apparently, what the actions were or how he considered them, which is not an answer to your question. You let him go. I don't know whether this is what you intended, but it certainly is not an answer to your question. So, therefore, Witness, you'll hear from Mr. Ivetic whether he wants an answer to his question or whether he wants you to go on to answer a question which was not asked, and then perhaps what that question would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if we could take it step by step. Could you tell us how did the other ethnic groups and ethnic parties react to these appointments by the SDA of Muslims to these key positions in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: In principle, since as far as this slicing of the cake was concerned, they were not pleased with the positions in the division of important positions in the MUP. So political parties were not satisfied but some agreement had been reached. That would be my answer. The one that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now these appointments of Muslims to key positions by the SDA, how did it affect the pre-existing ethnic distribution of officials within the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina that had existed in the years prior?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: During the previous years, the so-called ethnic criterion was seriously taken into consideration when dividing up posts in the ministry. However, that principle was infringed upon after the multi-party elections, especially from a professional point of view. The ethnic structure was also disrupted. SDA personnel started to dominate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you explain what you mean by saying that the "principle was infringed upon after the multi-party elections ... from a professional point of view." What did you mean in regard to that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: In the Ministry of Interior, it should be professionals that should be working there, people who were trained in law enforcement. When party people came to top positions in the Ministry of the Interior, then party people who were involved in politics cropped up, people who had no experience in law enforcement - I've just referred to Minister Delimustafic - people who had no experience in carrying out our responsible duties, and of course professionals who were there were taken aback, and it made it more difficult to carry out one's duties professionally and properly. It created difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now if we look at paragraph 9 on the same page in English and the next page in Serbian, you talk about reserve forces of the MUP that were activated but mostly Muslims. Was there any official justification that you heard while at the special unit explaining why so many reservists, mainly Muslims, were being activated?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: At that time, I was in a managerial position in one segment of the police, i.e., the special police, and it was a surprise for me to find out that in addition to the active-duty police force which had reached an enviable level of professionalism in peacetime, all of a sudden, a reserve force was also needed. It was surprising and somewhat inappropriate to see that true professionals, true special police needed a reinforcement to be efficient. There was no explanation for that. The commander just implemented what the ministry and the police administration ordered him to do, i.e.; to activate the reserve force of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in relation to paragraph 10 - and that's on page 3 in both versions - here, sir, you are telling us in relation to the special police unit that it was tasked outside its remit and especially in relation to actions to intimidate Serbs. Can you please be more specific as to why these tasks were outside the remit of the unit's activities and why you considered them unlawful.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The use of a special unit within the system of command of the Ministry of the Interior is within the remit of the minister. This unit is used very seldom, and when it is used, it is used for very special purposes, such as anti-terrorist combat, dealing with hostage situations in various situations, restoring public order, detailing with riots in prisons, and such very complex security tasks. In other words, they do what the regular police couldn't do. Unfortunately, during that period of time, we had an example when the special police was sent on a mission for very simple tasks that could have easily been carried out by other services affiliated with the Ministry of the Interior. Since we participated in several places in such actions against Serb individuals, groups, searching of their houses, for example, in Pale and Pofalici, we obviously could feel a reaction because our actions were fruitless. However, very quickly all of us, including me as an officer, realised that we were just a stick that was used against the people because we used inappropriate force, excessive force, the people revolted against that, obviously. A special example of that was Bilice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you said, as per your answer: "We obviously could feel a reaction because our actions were fruitless." Could you please explain what you meant when you said that your actions were fruitless?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: When they sent us to Bilice to find some large quantities of weapons apparently held by some people whose names I forget, we engaged a full special unit and mechanised equipment. We turned up there. Obviously there was no result achieved, no weapons were found. However, the people gathered. They protested. We were even blocked. They wouldn't allow us to return. The situation was dramatic. And then those people sent us a message, that it was pointless to use our unit for such tasks in view of the fact that there was a SJB there that could have easily implemented a task. That's why we were forced to seek explanation from the minister of the interior and from the senior staff there. Because they were the ones who very often exercised their right to send our unit on such missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was there ever any official justification received at the special unit from the MUP of why these activities were being ordered?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Sadly, no. In one paragraph, I explain why we had to hold a meeting with the MUP officials in the base in Krtelje. Because there was no explanation whatsoever. Obviously it was one-sided. One side wanted such things to happen on the ground. They wanted a special unit to flex its muscles and to show its full strength.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 11 of your statement, on the same page in both languages, you might have to scroll down on the Serbian original, you say that the special police unit was made to do military training instead of anti-terrorist training. Was there any justification or reason given for this change in training?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The Ministry of Interior does not discuss the -- the orders received by superiors. The principle of subordination has to function, which means that Vikic was in charge of training. He was the commander of that unit, and he said that in addition to our normal training we have to do some other kinds of training in order to complete our knowledge. It was a big surprise for us because we had already been in training for some other weapons and some other tools which, in principle, are used in exceptional situation and in war time. That was a conventional military training. We were trained to use Zoljas and Osas and other types of weapons. Something completely different than what we did when we were trained to deal with hostage situations and things like that. What we had formerly done was all of a sudden neglected and we had to do other things. In technical sense, special attention was not paid to tactical training but to tactical special training for military units, setting up ambushes and other such things. Obviously -- obviously we found that surprising and we realised that something dramatic was happening to the course of action and activities of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you've described that the training that your unit underwent. What kind of training was undertaken with respect to the special reserve of unit which had been activated of mostly Muslim reservists?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: That training was somewhat different. However, in essence it involved weapons used in exceptional circumstances and in war time. Those weapons were issued to us, and they were trained on those weapons and some lower levels of tactical training.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now if we could move on. Paragraph 13 of your statement, which is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, it's with some concern that I see that you're now at paragraph 13, it's a long statement, because you've used 28 minutes out of your 30 minutes, and apart from that I unfortunately had to establish that a lot of the answers are overlapping very much with the written statement. So, therefore, could you please wind up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we sent an e-mail adjusting the estimate for this witness to be one hour and 15 minutes. That was sent yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. After my proofing with the witness. And we don't intend to go through all the paragraphs of the statement, just to get some additional information as to ones that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That doesn't change at, the same time, if you ask for more specifics that the witness comes up with almost the same -- well, sometimes in slightly different language, but often the specifics are still not there. But we'll first verify when we received this information. Meanwhile, please could you try to speed up and avoid any overlaps, which I found there to be up to 70, 80 per cent of the answers of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I will try to speed it up. If we can look at paragraph 13 of the statement, and this is on page 4 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And here you're talking about the recruitment of the all Muslim special reserve unit. And when you say here: "When they were registered, it was noted that a number of people did not have identity documents," et cetera, who was it that was registering them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The headquarters of the Ministry of Interior was in charge of activating the reserve force. When people were employed, it was taken into account that people who were selected were sent to the Krtelje base where they would be trained as a future special police. When they first joined us, obviously we set up our records, and then we saw that some of the people did not have Bosnian documents. Some didn't even have IDs. We looked at the situation and we realised that there were a lot of people among them who were from Sandzak. They were from Muslims but they were from the Republic of Serbia. There were officers from them who were deserters and so on and so forth. And the rest, of course, is in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. So if we could move on so as to save time. If we turn to paragraph 16 in your statement, page 5 in English and the bottom of page 5 in the Serbian, and then it will bleed onto the next page in Serbian. And this is the meeting of the officers of the special unit with the Serb, Muslim, and Croat senior staff of the MUP, and you talked about an agreement being reached here and that the Muslim representatives did not adhere to that agreement. First of all, I'd like to ask you if you have any date reference or month reference for when this meeting would have taken place?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Unfortunately, it was a long time ago. Although I was a participant in all of these events, I can't remember the date. I'm sure that the meeting was held in a month preceding the beginning of war conflicts in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I really can't tell you exactly when. I did participate in the meeting. I can talk about that meeting. I can testify about it and add on what is already in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Without repeating what's already in your statement, was there anything else of significance that you recall being said at this meeting, especially from the Muslim participants of the same?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Of course, I remember. I will never forget when the officer of our special unit, Kemal Ademovic, took the floor. The rest of us officers said little. A lot more was said by the officers from the Ministry of the Interior who appeared to deal with the problem of the misuse of the special unit. I already told you what the problems were. They tried to set up the future work of the unit and its use in consensus with all the three representatives - the Serb, the Muslim, and the Croat - and this was advocated by the Serb representative because that solution would prolong the work of the unit on the condition that it was not misused. Kemal Ademovic was very negative and he spoke about the members of the JNA, which was the regular army in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, and he said that his children would never serve in that army. So if my colleague from my unit said that at an official unit, if could no longer contain the hatred against the Serbs who were a majority in the JNA, they even referred to the JNA as the Serb Chetnik Armada, it became clear to me that our further work together was impossible because there was a complete mistrust among the members of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to paragraph 19 and that will be on page 6 in the English, and I believe it's either at the bottom of the page or the next page in the Serbian, if we could scroll down. If we can scroll down in the Serbian. Okay. And if we could go to the next page, it's actually the next part of paragraph 19 I would like to reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the end of paragraph 19, you say: "Based on the agreement reached at the top of the MUP, the base in Vrace, in the MUP school, went to the Serbian part, and Muslim/Croat [sic] part of the specials remained there Krtelje." And then have you a reference to a document, which in our proceedings 1D5309, which is the transcript of the testimony of Alija Delimustafic in a case before the State Court of BiH. What is the reason that you cite to this testimony of this individual in relation to what is contained in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we, at the same time, have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. That would be then 1D5309.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you go ahead and answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: At the collegium of the ministers -- Minister of the Interior Alija Delimustafic, it was decided that the special unit of the then-Ministry of the Interior would be split because it had become impossible for them to work together. That situation would have certainly become a conflict some day and the decision was made that the -- old base in Vrace would be given to the Serbian part of the police, it would be pavilion F, more specifically; and that the other part of the special police would remain either in Krtelje or wherever they wanted. That decision was made at the collegium of the Ministry of the Interior. That was confirmed in a case which was heard before the Special Court in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we were aware of that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you assist us a bit in guiding us to the document where the relevant portion on the 16 pages is to be found? Or is it all over?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe it's in two sections. The witness showed me the B/C/S version when I was proofing him last night, and I'm now responding to the Prosecution's objections raised. I think for the sake of time I can at the break locate those and give them to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I think you have the gist of what the witness's testimony is, which is perhaps even more relevant at the present, but I will find those selections for you and advise you after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could turn back to D935, your statement, and if we can turn to page 7 in the English, and the bottom of 7 and it will bleed onto page 8 in the Serbian, and this is the -- describing the attack upon your unit when you tried to situate yourselves in the school compound as at Vrace. And towards the end of this paragraph -- I think it will be the next page in the B/C/S. There we go. We're fine in English. You say: "We released those attending the course, the leadership and the teaching staff, although we handed some of them over to the investigating authorities." First of all, I want to ask you how was the selection made of whom to hand over to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly switch off all unnecessary microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We managed to bring that to an end. At the end, we appointed very responsible people headed by Director Balic, and the commander who was in charge of a defence, and four or five people, two trainees, and some officers whose names I can't remember. We handed the -- the -- them over to the Pale station to establish how crimes were committed against our members. That was the criterion. The most responsible people among those who had waited for us there, who had all sorts of weapons, who had a plan in place, and who had prevented us from entering our base in Vrace according to the decision of Minister Delimustafic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now just to finish up with this incident, on paragraph 22 on page 8 in the English and between pages 8 and 9 in the Serbian, in these -- in this paragraph, you go into quite a bit of details --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We lost the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In this paragraph you go into quite a bit of details about the, quote/unquote, truth that you subsequently learned about these attacks. Can you tell us the source or sources from whom you learned of all the details that are contained in this paragraph about this attack?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The source of that information are statements taken by the legal bodies in the SJB in Pale. Those statements confirmed that there was a detailed plan to defend the centre. That was the name of that plan, apparently. That the person in charge was the director, Balic, who was a member of Minister Delimustafic's collegium, and that the forces within the centre were commanded by Dzevad Termiz. He was an officer who had been trained in the JNA, who was appointed by the MUP. He was well trained and very capable JNA officer. He had graduated from the military academy. When we entered the premises, as you can see in the statement, we personally saw the weapons that they had. They had facilities which were fortified for future combat and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the same. The witness gives very general answers to statements taken in Pale, not by whom, when, who gave those statements, and then within five seconds, moves to the substance rather than to your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you say "those statements taken by the legal bodies at the SJB Pale," first of all, from whom were those statements taken?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Dzevad Termiz and others were those who gave the statements. I was interested in the statement who was in command -- the person who was in command of the forces that were ordered to massacre us. In that statement, Dzevad Termiz gave a full account of the plan, activities, tools, weapons, and the tasks they had been given to prevent the entrance of the Serbian special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And who were the legal bodies at the SJB Pale to whom these -- who took these statements?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I was not present. That was done by professional members of the crime prevention police, most probably. Active-duty officers as part of their regular activities. They did that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, page 23, line 1, the answer starts with "and others." Was a name mentioned? I missed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There was. He mentioned the name Dzevad Termiz which is then at line 24 as well of page 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that statement recorded somewhere or what were the circumstances --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Termiz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the name Termiz in the statement of the witness. When was that statement taken? Witness, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say the date exactly, but it was four or five days after these people were taken to Pale for an investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And who --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact date. So it could have been the 9th or something like. I know that afterwards they were released, six days later. But, no, I was not in Pale, but did I get information from the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five days after what? Six days -- what year, what month approximately? I've got no idea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The month of April 1992. What happened in Vrace happened on the 5th of April. After the armed incident was over, they were arrested and handed over to Pale, and they spent a total of five or six days there and then they were exchanged. They were alive and well. No problems whatsoever. And that is when these statements came into being. I cannot tell you the exact day or hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you seen the statements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Dzevad Termiz's statement was made accessible to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it available to -- because we are now relying on this source of information which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is a copy in EDS. It is not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, for the Chamber always to be able to assess the reliability of the evidence, we're always very happy to receive documentary evidence which supports or at least is directly related to the statement of a witness or the testimony of a witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we are at the time for the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are at the time for the first break. Before we take that break, Witness, you've emphasised several times that -- I think it was Mr. Delimustafic who had a criminal record. Could you tell us what was on it? Was it -- what had been -- he had been convicted of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot exactly confirm, but there is a record of Mr. Delimustafic, and then that can be looked into. I believe that it is property-related crime, but I cannot confirm with certainty. But what is for sure is that the judiciary organs dealt with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has he been convicted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about these details. At any rate, we found out that our new minister had that kind of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, please answer my questions. So you don't know whether he was convicted, I do understand. Whatever you found out, apart from that, is not what I asked for. But if you say someone has a criminal record, that is commonly understood as someone being convicted by a court. So to say that that's a detail is not exactly my understanding of what it means if you say someone has a criminal record. But I leave it to that for the time being. We take break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we wait for the witness I can assist Your Honours with the citations that you were looking for earlier. In relation to 1D5309, the testimony of Alija Delimustafic, the second half of page 5 through the top of page 6, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could we have that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. 1D5309.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Page 5 in e-court, the bottom half. Beginning with Counsel Serdarevic and then it says Witness Delimustafic from there on to the first few lines on page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then also at page 7 until the middle of page 8 there's questioning by the accused Mandic on the same topic. And then the top of page 9 just a few lines talking about the work of the collegium by Mr. Delimustafic. Those would be, I think, the only selections that are directly relevant from the 16 pages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the statement of the witness in this respect is still comprehensible without having this underlying material, isn't it? Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it's -- presuming that it's an associated exhibits and the witness just said what the arrangement was for the -- where the police stations would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that -- whether others say that as well doesn't make it better comprehensible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the other issue I had was the -- you had asked about the statement of Mr. Termiz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. With some hesitation, I must say. I asked for it because it could support or specify what the witness said. There's still some doubt as to the relevance of the whole of the thing, so to seek further information in support of the witness's statement where the relevance is not entirely clear, of course I do that with some hesitation, but, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There are two - one handwritten, one typed - in e-court in the B/C/S language. The ERN of the handwritten is 0217-2714, and the ERN of the typewritten is 0217-2724. I'm not aware of an English translation of the same. Perhaps my colleagues on the other side might have more information since we got the document from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave in the hands of the parties whether they think that it would be useful to pay further attention to those, either for you in support or for the Prosecution challenging. Let move on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to page -- excuse me, if we could go back to D935, your statement, and page 9 in both language versions, and I would like to focus on paragraph 25 of the same. You talk about how -- while at Vrace you were subjected to daily attacks even with 60-, 82-, and 122-millimetre mortars from the Muslim side. Did the special police units incur any casualties from these daily attacks by the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, there were wounded persons. Unfortunately, there were fatalities as well. Not directly amongst the special police but one of the policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I get no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The microphone was on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muslim sniper hit us from Grbavica and this man was killed. There were quite a few members of the special police that were killed. I think that -- well, around us there was the Territorial Defence. We cannot confirm that. We cannot confirm the exact losses and the exact number of wounded persons, but among my own personnel that I commanded then, there weren't any casualties within that unit of ours. Day and night we were attacked by artillery, and even more often there were infantry attempts to take Vrace and the area that had already been under our control.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to page 10 in the English and page 11 in the Serbian, and paragraph 31 of your statement. Here, you are talking about the Zute Ose or Yellow Wasp paramilitary that you say refused to be subordinated to the command of the regular armed forces and wilfully conducted criminal conduct in Zvornik and harassed the local population. What was the ethnicity of those that were harassed by this paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The paramilitary group the Yellow Wasps in Zvornik practically took over completely. They had their own check-points. They had their own parapolice. They had their own individuals in groups that were looting and mistreating Serbs and Muslims. There were some of them there too, though in smaller numbers. The Ministry of the Interior did not believe it was in their interest for our young government to govern in that way and such activities were disallowed. After the minister's order, activity followed from the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska aimed at arresting and bringing to justice the paramilitaries involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did any other organs assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just ask for -- first of all, Mr. Ivetic, again the witness moves away from what you asked him. But I have one -- you said there were mistreating Serbs and Muslims. "There were some of them there too, though in smaller numbers." Who were there in smaller numbers? Are you referring to Muslims, are you referring to Serbs? Are you referring to member of the Yellow Wasps? What did you refer to when you said: "There were some of them there too, though in smaller numbers"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paramilitary group Yellow Wasps did not have any Muslims in their ranks. When I said "smaller number," I meant the Muslim population, but it was Serb civilians, the Serb population, that was tortured by this paramilitary group that did not have any Muslims within their ranks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And were Muslims tortured by them as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While preparing this action that I directly carried out with the special police and in co-operation with the military police, I think it was the 65th Protection Regiment. It's not that I think. They --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, why not answer my question rather than to tell us what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] I don't know about war crimes. It was their property-related crimes that were made known to me. They were looting. They were seizing whatever they could lay their hands on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again I was not asking about the character of the crimes committed. Where you emphasised that Serbs were victims, I asked you whether Muslims were tortured, were victims as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am talking about victims among all the inhabitants of Zvornik. I don't know the exact number and at this moment I cannot confirm that. I didn't know then exactly what the number was, but I know that they were looting, that they were stealing from people, that they were applying force against the population of Zvornik at their homes, at check-points, et cetera. Therefore, one could not live freely in the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you have knowledge about the Serbs being tortured by the Yellow Wasps. Now, do you know that it was exclusively Serbs or was everyone tortured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what you mean by the term "mucanje." Obviously we mean a different thing. I need to know what you mean by that word in order to be able to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are using an expression in a language I do not know. You said that Serbs were tortured by the Yellow Wasps. My question simply was: Was it just Serbs or were Muslims also tortured by the Yellow Wasps, and I invite you to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not mention the term "muciti." Perhaps we have an interpretation problem. I mentioned the word "maltretiranje."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The word used was "tortura."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then looting and mistreating, so I leave apart what exactly the crimes were or what it was exactly done by the Yellow Wasps. Were non-Serbs victims of that behaviour as well, including Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there were few Muslims in Zvornik then. However, if they were in Zvornik, then they were also a target of the Yellow Wasps. Everybody who was there had a problem with the Yellow Wasps. Everybody was a target. I don't know the exact numbers involved, but all the inhabitants of Zvornik had a problem with the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you're talking about smaller numbers, you are referring to a period where not the whole of the former Muslim population was still present in Zvornik or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the period when I had this operation of arresting a paramilitary formation. At that time I did not know exactly what the ethnic composition was and I wasn't particularly interested in that. I think that the majority were ethnic Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that the special police in co-operation with the military police, and specifically the 65th Protection Regiment, participated in the action to arrest the members of this paramilitary. How large was the paramilitary group which was being disarmed and arrested?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: According to our information, and later on that was confirmed during the arrests, the force involved was about that of a battalion or in numbers about 180, 170 men, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And ... why had not the local police taken care of this?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: The local police did not have the capacity. That is to say, they were not trained sufficiently, they did not have sufficient personnel levels to oppose a paramilitary formation that was armed with weapons that were supposed to be used in war operations, in combat. They didn't have the strength to do that, the local police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could now turn to page 13 in both languages of your statement and paragraph 38 of the same, and this is talking about 16 July 1995 when you arrived at Zvornik. And this paragraph of your statement says that you were briefed about the situation and problems concerning Zvornik. Can you be specific as to what exactly you were briefed on as to the situation and problems concerning Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: From Chief Vasic at the centre of security services, I was informed about the problems that the units were confronted with, the PJP units of the Ministry of Interior that were involved in the area of Zvornik. I am primarily referring to companies of PJPs, special police units from Doboj. And the information I received was that some people were taken prisoner, that a large column of Muslim soldiers who had not laid down weapons and surrendered in Srebrenica tried a breakthrough to Tuzla. I was told then that there were about 5.000 of them, that that was the estimate of these forces, and that they constitute a major danger for the army ant units of the Ministry of Interior that were resubordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska, that they were moving towards Tuzla, and that they took some of our policemen prisoners there. They didn't inform me of anything more or anything less. Those were the problems that I was informed about. Had I been informed about anything else, I probably would have written about that in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now prior to visiting Zvornik on this occasion you were at MUP staff in Pale. Can you tell us what your main activities or focus were at the staff in Pale during this time-period; that is, July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. My personal activity then had to do with a newly established staff of the police forces in Pale that was established, if I can remember exactly, sometime in mid-July or in the second half of July, and its direct task was - and that is why it was established on the basis of an order of the minister of the interior - because of the participation of police units at the Sarajevo front. At that time, at the Sarajevo front, there was a Muslim offensive that was raging against the Serb positions around Sarajevo and there was this major danger of the defences breaking down, and that would have had unforeseeable consequences for the civilian population primarily, the Serb population in Sarajevo, eastern Sarajevo. And the staff was established for the Sarajevo-Romanija area, to use military jargon. And I was a member of the staff most of the time in that area, and the headquarters of the staff was in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You are recorded as saying that the staff was established sometime in mid-July or the second half of July. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, you misspoke. The staff was established in mid-June or the second half of June. So it's not the month of July. It is the month of June 1995. June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I'm trying to seek some clarifications since the matter is addressed now. You say on the day when you arrived in Zvornik, you first went to the CJB where you were briefed about the situation, and you said that was mid-July 1995, if I understood you well. Now, we are usually making clear distinction between all the specific days in mid-July. Do you remember when in mid-July you arrived in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I arrived Zvornik on the 16th of July, 1995. I arrived at the security services centre in Zvornik. I communicated with the chief of that centre because I was the head of a sector who had arrived on the verbal order of the minister of the interior who has -- who had asked me to go on a mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I asked for a date, just for a date. Was that the same day when, as you said, you had received a verbal order from Mr. Kovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in answering one of my prior questions, you talked about the offensive against Serb positions around Sarajevo, and you said that there was a major danger of the defences breaking down and that would have been unforeseeable consequences for the civilian populations. What kinds of consequences were you dealing with at the time that you were at the staff in Pale that would result from the Muslim offensive?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I spent most of my time over there in touring Sarajevo municipalities. That's where the brigades of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps were deployed and the units of the Ministry of the Interior were resubordinated to them. They fought to preserve defence positions there. I monitored the situation in some of those municipalities. In some of the municipalities, the situation was very complex. It was difficult to hold on. In some, the situation was better. However, I also inspected some civilian structures because in the zone of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, there was a state of war declared, so I inspected the staffs, the civilian staffs, and I was informed by the presidents of the Crisis Staffs of those municipalities about the civilian situation. Because if the defence lines were too full, I would have had to activate Plan B which was the evacuation of the population. That would have made the situation very complicated. It would have compounded the situation even further, which is why we had to monitor developments constantly, 24/7. If I may continue, I would like to add another sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ask Mr. Ivetic whether you moved away from his question or whether he thinks it still is within.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask a question and see if you can answer that in one sentence: How many civilians are we talking about in terms of the population that, under Plan B, would have to be evacuated if the Muslim offensive broke through the lines?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Well, if we're talking about the Serbian population in the then Serbian Sarajevo, we're talking about 150.000 Sarajevo civilians, Serbs, who were residing in the territory of all Sarajevo municipalities. If the line had fallen down and the action by the Muslim forces was launched from within the city -- the 1st Corps of the BiH Army was active all the time day and night, there were infantry attacks, sniper attacks, they opened fire on every position, every different position of the Army of Republika Srpska. However -- let me finish. There was also another ring which was in the direction of Central Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I stop you there. You asked again and again to finish. You can finish an answer to the question. Mr. Ivetic told you that if you could answer in one line, he would appreciate that. You gave the number. That's it. Therefore, as long as you stay within the context of the question, you can continue. If you move away from that, we'll stop you. Mr. Ivetic, just for you to know that you've three minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think my last question will be just to have you briefly again, sir, please explain what you mean when you say there was another ring. And that will be my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if Mr. Mladic wants to consult with counsel. He has an opportunity to do so but at inaudible volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not inaudible. Could you please ... Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud. I again insist on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can then instead ask: Was there any international agreements in place on the territory of Sarajevo for either cease-fire or demilitarisation of that area at the time of this Muslim offensive that you've identified?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I can't remember any of the agreements, but I know that the Muslim offensive lasted for 22 days both from the inner ring as well as the outer ring, but I can't remember exactly what kind of agreements were in place at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're doing exactly the same again. You start saying "I can't remember," and then you draw our attention to matters which you consider relevant. But it's Mr. Ivetic who puts the questions, so would you please refrain from doing that again and again and again. Mr. Ivetic, you said this was your last question. The witness doesn't remember. Is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then that's my last question. I think he has now completed what he was talking about about the rings, so I think that all that I wanted on the record is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On behalf of my client and the rest of the team, I thank you for answering my questions today, sir. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Ms. Pack, are you ready to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, you'll now be examined by Ms. Pack. You'll find her to your right. Ms. Pack is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed. And I again, Mr. Karisik, I again remind you that you should focus your answer on the questions put to you, and if you go beyond that, we'll stop you. And we're not inclined to do that 10 or 20 times, so please keep that in the back of your mind. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, just to go back through your various positions you held. From April 1992, commander of the 1st Special Police Unit of the RS MUP, known as the police detachment, then later in 1992 you became commander of the special police brigade, which is what the special unit became; yes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: By July 1995 you were head of the public security department of MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: First the chief of the police administration for a while, and then I was appointed the head of the public security department in November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Under Tomislav Kovac in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes. He had a higher position in the Ministry of the Interior. He was above me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your counterpart then in July 1995, Dragan Kijac, head of the State Security Department; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You ended up after the war as deputy minister?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: When was that were you appointed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I believe you'll find it in my statement. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You talk in your statement, paragraph 6, you don't need to look at it, you talk about the outstanding professionals in the special unit before the war. You, yourself, you regard yourself as an outstanding professional in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you whenever you mention a paragraph, whenever you want to discuss a paragraph and display it, can it be enlarged in the B/C/S version, for my benefit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I don't want to discuss it. I'm asking, do you regard yourself as an outstanding professional in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes, an outstanding professional in the special police unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack. Witness, it's my recollection that you were provided with a hard copy of your own statement, so if any reference is made to any paragraph, you received that. So you always can have a look at it if it's -- if it's not well visible on the screen for you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You were highly trained and you were promoted to general by the end?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes. By a decree of the president on the proposal of the Ministry of Interior in compliance with the Law on the Internal Affairs, all officers were promoted within the MUP. A certain number of us were promoted and became generals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no one asked you about others. Now you really have to stick to the question because finally the Chamber may come to a point where we just do not accept you moving away and expanding on questions. That should be clear to you. The simple answer was yes, and if you added "by a decree of the president," that is already beyond what was asked, on the proposal of whom was also not what was asked. Perhaps I would not have stopped you there. But if you then say what happened to others, then you really move far away from the question. Please stick to the question. And as I said before, we're not going to remind you 10 or 20 times and waste our time on listening to what was not asked. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'd like to clarify paragraph 19 of your witness statement which is in front of you, so you can have a look at it. It's about division of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, it's 1D04749a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is now D935.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we can just to e-court, for the English it's page 6 and the B/C/S it's page 6 to 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: But you have the B/C/S in front of you. Just looking at this paragraph 19, you tell us about halfway down: "That is why we were relieved when a dispatch arrived about the splitting of the MUP, which was signed by Mr. Momcilo Mandic in his capacity as authorised official. This was agreed and co-ordinated at the level of leadership of the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina in keeping with the treaty of Lisbon/Cutileiro Plan." I was going to ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Could we have please P3009 up. Now it's one page in the B/C/S. Two pages in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And what you could see in the B/C/S at the bottom. Might not be able to see it now, but it's signed by Mandic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I can see Momcilo Mandic's signature. To be honest, I am in a position -- in no position to tell you whether this is, indeed, his signature or not. But that's how it's signed: Mr. Momcilo Mandic, and there's a signature. I don't know if it's indeed his or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. The date is the 31st of March. It's addressed, you can see, to the minister, to the SJBs, to the CSBs, et cetera. It's the dispatch to which you refer in paragraph 19; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, you should add the year, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: 31st of March, 1992. And now please if you just look at the end of this first paragraph where it starts: "In order to conduct internal affairs on the territory of the Republic of Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Ministry of Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina based in Sarajevo is setting up the following Security Services Centres..." And it goes on. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: If I have to discuss the dispatch, I would need to read it, and for that, the entire document should be enlarged. This is a dispatch sent by the then-deputy minister of the interior. I'm in no position to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked whether you saw what Ms. Pack read to you. Apparently you do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: If -- in fact, we can enlarge the second paragraph in the B/C/S. And you can read that.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Give me a moment, please, to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I'll read it out: "Within the above-mentioned Security Services Centres, in order to carry out specific tasks and duties within the competence of the organs of internal affairs, public security stations are set up for the territories of municipalities." Then: "On the day this law comes into force, the Security Services Centres and public security stations of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina MUP on the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina are abolished and cease to function and their authority, i.e., tasks and duties within the competence of organs of internal affairs are taken over by the above-mentioned organisational units of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Have you read that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mandic declared in this dispatch on the 31st of March, 1992, that from the 1st of April republican CSB and SJB stations would cease to function and would be taken over by Bosnian Serb CSBs and SJBs; right? That's a what it says?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: Yes. You have now read one part of the dispatch. I can see a very minuscule version of that text. But I would not discuss anything that was sent by Mr. Momcilo Mandic. That should be a question for him. And what is your question for me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, wait for a question. Second, whether it's a question for you or for Mr. Mandic is not for you decide but is for Ms. Pack to decide. If you don't know the answer, just tell us. If you do know the answer, irrespective of whether you thought it would be better put to someone else, answer the question. Please proceed, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, I'm trying to clarify what you say in your own statement at paragraph 19 where you say you refer to this dispatch. You say this happened as a result of a signed agreement, the Cutileiro Plan or the Treaty of Lisbon, as you call it, and that it was agreed by the republican MUP leadership; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: My answer is that this part which refers to the special police is the only part I can comment upon. I can't comment upon the rest of the dispatch. As far as our special police are concerned ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Right. So would it surprise you to learn that there is no such thing as the Lisbon treaty and that the so-called Cutileiro Plan that you refer to here in paragraph 19 was a statement of principles described as the "basis of future negotiations," dated 18th of March, 1992? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: I knew that there was a dispatch issued by Mr. Momcilo Mandic. We also knew that the Cutileiro Plan had been issued. That's all we knew.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you, please, to look at another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: It is 65 ter 10750.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And you can see on the B/C/S at page 1, it's -- in the English translation at page 2 it is from Alija Delimustafic, the minister of the republican MUP. You can see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: No, B/C/S page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be enlarged? Do you want the first part or the second part, Ms. Pack.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I want to go to the second part, please. Second and third paragraphs I'll be looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you read it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: So this is dated the 31st --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked the witness if he could read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you read the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, but it will take some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can read it. It's large enough. That was my question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. So we this -- it's for Alija Delimustafic, it's dated at the top there 31st of March, 1992, same day as the dispatch from Mandic, and it's to all the MUP administrations. You can see that at the top. The SDB, the CSB, SJBs, SMs, the police stations; right? And just briefly at paragraph 1, the first paragraph, it's English page 1 in the first paragraph, B/C/S, same page, briefly that paragraph refers, doesn't it, you can see the reference number in the name to the Mandic dispatch I've just shown you in the middle of that paragraph; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karisik, do you agree that reference is made to the dispatch we just looked at which was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there's a reference to a dispatch. I can see it written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see that Minister Delimustafic makes reference to Mr. Momcilo Mandic's dispatch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay. And in the English, please, page 2, B/C/S same page, it's the second paragraph I'm going to read.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: He says: "Finally, I would like to take this opportunity to again express my belief that the greatest number of MUP workers wish to work in a united MUP and that they find any segregation, especially on a national basis, difficult. Do not allow anyone to separate you from your work colleagues, because there are countless examples of mutual solidarity and sacrifice for others in carrying out security tasks even in conditions in which their execution endangers one's ... life."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: "One's own life."

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: "One's own life." Thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Were you aware that Delimustafic the republican minister did not agree to the abolishment of the republican CSBs and SJBs or to the division of the MUP upon national or ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO KARISIK
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. I have not seen this dispatch before at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to admit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number P7212, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Now I'd like to show you P00406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it. Could I ask the witness -- Witness, in your statement you say that this was an action which was agreed upon. Now you're shown another dispatch issued by Delimustafic which says the contrary. On what basis did you state that it was agreed upon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of a decision of Mr. Delimustafic's collegium. I stated that the division of the special police entailed division of their headquarters. I've not seen this dispatch before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the one document you referred to in your statement doesn't say anything about an agreement, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are the pages numbers that I had directed you to and this is the document the Prosecution objected as being not -- well, they objected to the admission of it, so it's not been admitted. It's 1D5310. And again, the page numbers I had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you say that those portions of it do support that. Of course, I only had a glance to it. If I have read them not sufficiently accurately, then I'll do that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They discussion the whole development of the situation through the collegium and that, specifically pages 9 and 10, the minister says nothing can be done without an [Overlapping speakers] ... collegium.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll have a further look at it and perhaps read it in more detail. That's one of the problems the Judges have, that they are presented with documents of several pages and we only received the relevant information when we came back to court. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this is the extracts from the book, "Sarajavan [phoen] Roulette," I take it, that my friend is giving evidence about its content that he didn't take the witness to. But I'm unclear --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The testimony --

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- of Minister Alija Delimustafic, the man who authored the dispatch that you had on the screen previously, 5D -- pardon me, 1D5309.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the 16-page extract not only the statement of Delimustafic, as you told us, but also a statement of I think the accused in that case. But at least recordings of proceedings of which the Chamber is not aware exactly what the proceedings were about in 2007, but at least there were proceedings apparently, before I take it, the state court because I saw a reference made to judges, international judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
